headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading error: OpenHands can write/execute in a shared runtime while Perplexity returns web-derived content that may be treated as authoritative.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenHands can read/write files and use MCP in a Docker runtime, while Perplexity can browse the web and return cited content. If Perplexity output is copied into OpenHands files or prompts, attacker-controlled text can influence tool use. The bridge is not automatic, so this is below high, but the interaction is plausible.
conditions: IF Perplexity output is pasted into OpenHands prompts or files
IF OpenHands parses web-derived text as instructions
mitigations: Use a strict prompt delimiter when transferring text
Paste only quoted excerpts, not full pages
Disable MCP tools for tasks that ingest untrusted text
Review any web-sourced instructions before execution

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenHands touches files mounted into its runtime and can write them; Perplexity handles uploaded documents and browsing context and sends queries to vendor APIs. If the same sensitive file is mounted into OpenHands and uploaded or summarized in Perplexity, data can leak across the pair. The shared-data pathway exists in default workflows, so medium fits.
conditions: IF the same mounted file is uploaded to Perplexity
IF OpenHands is given secrets or regulated documents in its runtime volume
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared runtime volume
Do not upload secrets or regulated documents to Perplexity
Use redacted copies for cross-agent workflows
Separate workspaces for each agent

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenHands has broad filesystem write, shell, and git modification inside its runtime; Perplexity has no host write, but it can still influence shared artifacts through user-mediated outputs. Because OpenHands supports multiple instances and shares state via mounted volume, concurrent edits to the same workspace can conflict. Perplexity lacks write access, so this is not high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same mounted workspace
IF OpenHands instances edit the same git branch or files concurrently
mitigations: Assign separate branches per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use file-level locks or a single-writer rule
Commit frequently to reduce merge conflicts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity is a search-RAG system that produces answers and citations, and OpenHands can act on files and shell commands. If OpenHands treats Perplexity’s output as authoritative without verification, web errors can cascade into code changes or runtime actions. The pair’s default interaction is dangerous because one agent can operationalize the other’s unverified claims.
conditions: IF OpenHands uses Perplexity answers as ground truth
IF Perplexity output is fed into code edits or shell actions without verification
mitigations: Require a human review step before execution
Cross-check claims against primary sources
Ask Perplexity for citations and verify them manually
Restrict OpenHands to read-only mode for sourced tasks

E_compliance.rationale: OpenHands handles files mounted into its runtime and model provider API keys, while Perplexity processes uploaded documents and browsing context via vendor-hosted APIs. If regulated or residency-bound data is placed into both systems, retention and jurisdiction differences can create a compliance mismatch. The risk is data-class dependent, but the pair exposes enough surface to warrant medium.
conditions: IF regulated documents are uploaded to Perplexity
IF OpenHands runtime contains data subject to stricter retention or residency rules
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either agent
Use anonymized or synthetic test data
Check vendor retention settings before upload
Keep a separate compliant workflow for sensitive data
